chain_trace.break_detail: Contract gap: No constraint in structured_contract.json defines scroll offset parameter semantics. Missing constraint: 'scroll offset=0 returns first point, offset=N returns point at position N+1 (0-indexed array semantics) OR offset returns starting point_id=N (point_id-based semantics)'. Observed behavior indicates offset is point_id-based (offset=5 returns point_id=5 first), which contradicts conventional 0-indexed pagination expectation where offset=5 would skip first 5 items.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: ScrollRequestInternal.offset is Option<PointIdType>, not usize. PointIdType is ExtendedPointId enum (NumId(u64) or Uuid). Comment says 'Start ID to read points from' - this confirms offset is point_id-based (inclusive lower bound), not array index-based. If offset=Some(NumId(5)), scroll starts returning from point_id=5 onward, not skipping first 5 results. Observed behavior (offset=5 returns [5,6,7]) matches source design: offset is point_id inclusive lower bound.
source_grounding.note: Source code confirms ScrollRequestInternal.offset is Option<PointIdType> with comment 'Start ID to read points from'. PointIdType is ExtendedPointId (NumId(u64) | Uuid). This design means offset is an inclusive lower bound on point_id, not a skip-count. offset=5 means 'start from point_id=5', not 'skip first 5 points'. This is by-design behavior: scroll offset is point_id-based cursor, not array-index-based skip count. The defect report's expectation of 0-indexed array semantics (offset=5 returns [6,7,8]) assumes different design than source implements.

mundane_explanation.note: Observed offset behavior (offset=5 returns point_id 5 first) is by-design per source: ScrollRequestInternal.offset is PointIdType (inclusive lower bound), not usize skip count.
